elements.texte:
[cheerful] The carrier announces a delay on the next deliveries.

Customer service wants to call the customers concerned to let them know.

Concerned: the customers with an order being processed.

To call them, we get their first name, last name and phone number from the customers table.

But how do we know which customers have an order being processed?

elements.texte:
[cheerful] First try: filter the customers table on the order’s status.

Error: the customers table has no status column.

The status has to be found elsewhere: in the orders table.

Each order also keeps its customer’s ID there: customer underscore ID.

So we first need to find the customers concerned in the orders table.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] A subquery is a query placed inside another one.

It provides a result that the main query uses, for example to filter the data.

Run on its own, this query returns the IDs of the customers (customer underscore ID) with an order being processed.

It returns a list of customer IDs: 4, 1, 3 and 5.

The list also contains a null: order number 16 has no customer.

This query then goes in parentheses, right after in.

This way, in receives the list built by the subquery.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] In tests each customer, one by one: is their ID in the list?

Sophie Martin’s ID (1) is in the list returned by the subquery:

So her row is kept in the result.

Lucas Bernard’s ID (2) isn’t in the list returned by the subquery:

So his row doesn’t appear in the result.

Likewise, Emma Dubois, Nathan Petit and Chloé Moreau are in the list.

The five other customers are left out: their ID isn’t in the list.

The null doesn’t match any customer: it changes nothing here.

Result: 4 customers are kept.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] The subquery returns a list of IDs.

With in, the main query keeps only the customers whose ID is in this list.

The result shows the first name, last name and phone number

Of the 4 customers with at least one order being processed.

Customer service now has the four numbers to call.

This way, every customer concerned will be told about their order’s delay.
